claims.statement: The fragment distinguishes enterprise access through personal accounts on the website with optional additional SAML restrictions from IdP-provisioned and controlled Enterprise Managed Users. Optional SAML is scoped to the personal-account model, not an EMU exemption or universal security recommendation; no enterprise identity model or configuration was verified.

A recovery code is described as an enterprise-access fallback when SAML configuration errors or IdP problems prevent SAML SSO. The fragment supplies no eligible role, code generation, custody, expiry or tested recovery sequence; it does not establish available codes or authorize reading or using credentials.

The fragment only points to the setup-user concept page. It supplies no setup-user lifecycle, entitlement, credential or role requirements on its own; the linked full page is not marked reviewed through this pointer.
The EMU-named fragment gives profile-picture navigation to Enterprise. This UI step is not evidence of a managed account, enterprise membership, entitlement or successful access.

The GHES fragment gives profile-picture navigation to Enterprise settings. This is distinct from Cloud and EMU menu labels but does not prove administrator permissions, a reachable instance or any settings mutation.

The Cloud navigation fragment opens Enterprise Cloud and uses the profile menu, with Enterprise or Enterprises followed by enterprise selection depending on environment. Singular and plural paths are contextual alternatives, not an actual enterprise inventory, access test or universal menu guarantee.
